description: We are a team interested in AI, machine learning, software, and data. For the Flame in Freefall challenge, we want to explore how AI and data tools can help make microgravity combustion research easier to understand and compare. We welcome teammates interested in physics, combustion or space science, scientific data analysis, and visualization.
summary:
**OrbitAI LaB** is an AI-powered research platform designed to make NASA’s microgravity combustion data easier to explore, understand, and apply to space fire safety.

NASA has collected valuable fire experiments in space, but finding and comparing useful information across different investigations can be difficult and time-consuming.

Our platform brings NASA experimental data into one interactive dashboard. Researchers can search and rank investigations, compare experimental conditions, explore flame behavior through 3D visualization, and use a Gemini-powered AI assistant to understand scientific findings. Our unique **Evidence Twin** feature allows users to enter conditions such as oxygen level, pressure, fuel material, and ventilation to identify potential fire hazards, supporting evidence, and important engineering checks.

OrbitAI LaB helps researchers turn complex experimental records into understandable insights that can support safer spacecraft, future Moon and Mars habitats, and fire-safety innovations on Earth.

Our vision is to expand the platform with more NASA research, improved AI retrieval, and scientifically validated predictive models.
details:
Project Details — OrbitAI LaB

OrbitAI LaB is an AI-powered research platform developed by our team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Flame in Freefall challenge. Our goal is to turn complex NASA microgravity combustion data into useful insights that support fire safety in space.

What Does Our Project Do?

NASA has collected valuable fire experiment data, but finding, comparing, and understanding these records can be difficult. OrbitAI LaB brings experimental information into one interactive platform.

Our website provides five main features:

  1. NASA Investigation Explorer: Helps researchers search and rank relevant combustion experiments.
  2. Experiment Comparison: Allows users to compare fuels, oxygen levels, pressure, airflow, and available experimental results.
  3. Evidence Twin: Our unique feature lets researchers enter environmental conditions and identify potential fire hazards, supporting NASA evidence, missing information, and recommended engineering checks.
  4. AI Insights: Uses Google's Gemini AI to explain scientific information using relevant NASA experimental records.
  5. 3D Visualization: Helps users explore how flame behavior may change under different environmental conditions.

How Did We Build It?

We developed the platform using:

  • React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for the interactive website.
  • Python and FastAPI for backend processing and NASA data retrieval.
  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets as our scientific data source.
  • Google Gemini API for AI-assisted explanations.
  • Three.js for interactive 3D visualizations.
  • Local evidence retrieval and rule-based analysis to provide basic functionality without relying entirely on an online AI service.

Our system organizes NASA experimental records, retrieves relevant information, calculates descriptive statistics, and presents findings in a format researchers can understand.

What Makes OrbitAI LaB Creative?

Our innovation is the Evidence Twin, which connects real experimental evidence with conditions researchers want to investigate.

Instead of only displaying NASA data, our platform helps users ask practical questions, compare experimental conditions, identify possible hazards, and understand what additional testing may be needed.

We combine scientific data exploration, AI assistance, interactive visualization, and fire-hazard screening in one platform.

Benefits and Intended Impact

OrbitAI LaB aims to reduce the time researchers spend searching for relevant experiments and help them make better use of NASA's existing research.

Our project can support future research into fire safety aboard spacecraft, space stations, and Moon and Mars habitats. The findings may also inspire improvements in fire detection, protective materials, and fire-safety technologies on Earth.

Current Limitations and Future Development

We recognize that spacecraft fire safety requires reliable scientific evidence. Our current platform provides evidence-based screening, not certified safety decisions or validated numerical fire predictions. Some NASA records also have missing measurements.

With three additional months, we plan to organize more NASA datasets and scientific publications, improve evidence retrieval, train and validate specialized machine-learning models where sufficient data exists, and expand offline research capabilities.

Our vision is to make NASA's combustion research easier to access, understand, and apply—helping researchers build a safer future in space and on Earth.
